## Teaching philosophy

::: {.section-intro}
I approach mathematics, statistics, and data science teaching as an activity of understanding, practice, and communication. Courses are designed to help students produce reproducible analyses, justify their choices, and explain their results clearly.
:::

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-panel}
### Active learning

Classes emphasize hands-on work, applied situations, and projects where statistical concepts are used in concrete contexts.
:::

::: {.feature-panel}
### Reproducibility

Activities use R, Quarto, GitHub, and explicit project structures so that reasoning, code, and results can be checked.
:::

::: {.feature-panel}
### Support

Exercises, formative feedback, course assistants, and CDA resources support autonomy while preserving the central role of student understanding.
:::
:::

## Teaching experience and languages

I teach at undergraduate and graduate levels at Université Laval and UQAC. My experience covers probability, applied statistics, data science, R programming, visualization and project management.

- GSO-6092, *Project Management*: graduate course taught in English in Winter 2026 and Fall 2026 (in progress).
- GSO-6082, Gestion de projets: partial assignment of 21 teaching hours in Fall 2026, replacing the regular instructor from August 31 to October 16.
- STT-1900: in-person and online teaching and coordination for approximately 350 students in 2025.

In assessments, I ask students to justify their choice of methods, verify computations and interpret uncertainty. When AI tools are permitted, their use must be disclosed and their output checked. My [published discussion in the Journal of Data Science (2026)](https://doi.org/10.6339/26-JDS1208H) addresses AI-generated assignments.

## Supervision {#supervision}

I have served as faculty consultant for three undergraduate projects on directional statistics (2024), random matrices (2025) and visual inference (2026). I have also supervised industry internships and undergraduate research projects at UQAC, and examined two master’s theses.

My approach to supervision emphasizes a focused question, explicit milestones, version control and reproducible analysis. My [research themes](recherche.qmd) provide training topics in simulation, diagnostics, visualization and software development.

## Academic coordination and curriculum development

At the CDA, I coordinate and train approximately 30 teaching assistants supporting mathematics and statistics courses. I develop diagnostic assessments to identify learning needs early and guide student support.

I contribute to the review of the statistics degree and the development of Université Laval’s bachelor’s program in statistics and data science. I also contribute to the co-adaptation of *Probabilités et statistique, Science et génie*, fourth edition, forthcoming from TC Média Livres in April 2027.

[GPT-CDA](cda/index.qmd) received two PAIP teaching innovation grants, in 2025 and 2026, of CAD 20,000 each. Open resources, including [tutorizeR](packages/tutorizeR.qmd), datasets and tutorials, extend this training work.

## Teaching recognition

I received Teaching Stars recognition from the Faculty of Science and Engineering for 2022-2023, 2023-2024, 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, as well as the Professor Star Award in 2014. In 2026, I also received student recognition in the teaching award category at the Gala du mérite.

[FSG Teaching Stars ceremony](https://www.fsg.ulaval.ca/faculte/evenements-facultaires/ceremonie-des-etoiles-de-lenseignement-fsg){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
